holidays.name: International Stuttering Awareness Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to raising public awareness about stuttering, celebrating people who stutter, and encouraging patience, listening, and understanding in everyday conversation.
holidays.origin: Established in 1998 by the International Stuttering Association and the International Fluency Association, with the first observance held in 1998 and grassroots events held worldwide since.
holidays.funFact: Roughly 1 in 100 adults stutters, and famous people who stutter include actor James Earl Jones, singer Ed Sheeran, and President Joe Biden.

holidays.name: National Nut Day
holidays.description: A crunchy celebration of all things nutty, from almonds and pecans to peanuts and pistachios. Fans are encouraged to snack on, bake with, or simply admire nuts in every form.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance, popularly marked on October 22 in the United States, created to celebrate nuts and their health benefits as the fall harvest season peaks.
holidays.funFact: Botanically, peanuts aren't true nuts at all. They are legumes that grow underground, making them cousins of peas and beans.

holidays.name: Caps Lock Day
holidays.description: A loud and proud tongue-in-cheek holiday where people are invited to TYPE IN ALL CAPS FOR THE DAY, celebrating the key that makes everything feel like SHOUTING.
holidays.origin: Created in 2000 by Derek Arnold of Iowa as a joke to honor the Caps Lock key, and later spread by humor-loving internet communities. It is said to have been chosen because it was the birthday of his fictional character, Caps Lock.
holidays.funFact: The Caps Lock key descends from the typewriter's Shift Lock, a mechanical lever that physically locked the typebasket into the upper position.

holidays.name: Color Me Happy Day
holidays.description: A cheerful day to brighten your world with bright colors, whether by wearing something vibrant, coloring in a coloring book, or painting a room, with the goal of boosting everyone's mood.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance rooted in color psychology, encouraging people to surround themselves with joyful colors as the days grow shorter and darker in autumn.
holidays.funFact: Studies on color psychology suggest yellow is the color most associated with happiness, though research on how colors affect mood is still debated.

holidays.name: Cranky Co-Workers Day
holidays.description: A day to practice extra patience and kindness with the grumpiest people at the office, perhaps with a coffee offering or a friendly smile as a peace treaty.
holidays.origin: An unofficial workplace observance, said to be a humorous way to acknowledge that everyone has bad days, and to remind us to extend compassion to colleagues.
holidays.funFact: Surveys have found that a significant share of employees say a rude coworker is one of the top sources of workplace stress, so this holiday is surprisingly practical.
